sources.title: 10 Agentic AI Concepts You Need to Master Before 2027

concepts.title: Harness engineering
concepts.evidence: The model is only one component. A production harness supplies prompts, model routing, tool access through MCP or equivalent interfaces, sandboxed execution, state, retries, validation, and observability. The article frames reliability as a systems problem rather than a prompt-only problem.
details: Use sandboxed runtimes for code execution.
Treat prompt, tools, state, validation and tracing as one engineered runtime.

concepts.title: Loop engineering
concepts.evidence: An agent repeatedly observes, reasons, acts and receives consequences. Reliable loops need observable outcomes, verification, bounded retries, explicit iteration and cost ceilings, failure classification, and a termination rule enforced in code.
warnings: A request in the prompt to stop is weaker than an enforced ceiling.
Unbounded retry loops can spend indefinitely without improving.

concepts.title: Context engineering
concepts.evidence: Context is a deliberately assembled working set, not a dump of everything available. More tokens can reduce performance when irrelevant or stale information competes with current constraints. Retrieval, compression, ordering and deletion are core operations.
details: Select information for the current decision.
Preserve current goals, constraints and state.
Remove stale tool output and redundant prose.

concepts.title: Tool design
concepts.evidence: Tool reliability depends on narrow, unambiguous names, schemas and descriptions. Overlapping tools or loosely defined arguments make the model choose the wrong operation or emit unparsable calls. Validation and useful error messages allow recovery.
warnings: Do not expose a giant ambiguous tool surface.
Do not blame the model before inspecting tool schemas and error feedback.

concepts.title: Memory architecture
concepts.evidence: Memory should retain durable decisions, rationales, preferences and unresolved work—not entire transcripts. The design must distinguish working context from long-term memory and provide retrieval, update, deduplication and expiry policies.

concepts.title: Orchestration patterns
concepts.evidence: Useful patterns include sequential pipelines, routing, parallel fan-out, evaluator/optimizer loops and supervisor/worker structures. Multi-agent diagrams are easy to over-apply; add agents only when roles, contexts or tools genuinely need separation.
warnings: A single capable agent plus tools is often simpler.

concepts.title: Guardrails and permissions
concepts.evidence: Use least privilege, allowlists for known-safe operations, explicit approval for irreversible actions, sandboxing, limits and audit logs. Guardrails should be enforced outside the model where possible.

concepts.title: Agent evaluations
concepts.evidence: Traditional exact-output tests do not cover nondeterministic, multi-step agents. Evaluate task completion, tool choice, trajectory quality, safety, cost, latency and recovery over a representative scenario set; retain traces to diagnose regressions.

concepts.title: Human-in-the-loop design
concepts.evidence: Human involvement should be placed at high-risk, ambiguous or irreversible decision points. Too many approvals cause fatigue and rubber-stamping, so gates must be meaningful and present enough evidence for a quick decision.

concepts.title: Observability and tracing
concepts.evidence: Capture prompt/model versions, tool calls and results, state transitions, latency, token/cost data, errors and final outcomes. Historical traces turn questions about a bad run into queries and enable replay, comparison and root-cause analysis.

images.meaning: Concept illustrations and section graphics; useful only when they clarify the system layer or loop, not as decorative article banners.
images.review: Manual visual triage required because extracted image objects include page furniture.

uncertainties: Ligatures and punctuation are occasionally corrupted in extracted text.
Page 17 is a resource list, not an additional core concept.

sources.title: 15 Agentic AI Concepts Everyone Needs
sources.extractionQuality: medium; readable meaning with severe intra-word spacing on some pages

concepts.title: Agent as a persistent goal
concepts.evidence: A one-shot task returns an answer; an agent owns a goal and continues choosing actions until a stopping condition is met. The article grounds later concepts in a newsletter analytics goal.

concepts.title: Observe-decide-act-check loop
concepts.evidence: The worked analytics sequence pulls performance data, compares it with a target, acts on the weakest subject line or segment, then checks evidence again. The check stage is what distinguishes iterative work from a single prompt.
concepts.example: Review newsletter performance: pull open/click data, compare against thresholds, identify the weakest result, propose or apply one change, then re-check.

concepts.title: Planning and task decomposition
concepts.evidence: Split work where real dependencies exist and show each step rather than leaping to a conclusion. Do not manufacture a complex plan for a simple independent task.
concepts.prompt: Show your work for each step separately. Do not skip to the final answer.

concepts.title: Reflection as a measurable rule
concepts.evidence: Reflection should compare output with a criterion or evidence, not ask whether the result merely feels good. A correction loop needs a concrete discrepancy to fix.

concepts.title: Tool use
concepts.evidence: A language model can advise, while an agent with tools can fetch data, modify artifacts and verify results. Grant only the tools required for the goal and make outputs observable.

concepts.title: Selective memory
concepts.evidence: Decide deliberately what carries into future runs. A stateless analytics calculation may need no durable memory; preferences, decisions or recurring operating rules may.

concepts.title: Context-window management
concepts.evidence: Context is finite; include current goal, necessary data, constraints and prior decisions, while excluding irrelevant history. Overflow and noise reduce reasoning quality.

concepts.title: Explicit state management
concepts.evidence: Multi-step work needs a machine-readable record of what is pending, in progress, completed or blocked so the agent does not confuse conversation history with current state.

concepts.title: Guardrails
concepts.evidence: Define rules the agent cannot cross, such as not publishing, sending, deleting or changing client-facing material without validation.

concepts.title: Permissions and human approval
concepts.evidence: Permission boundaries decide which actions are automatic and which require review. Client-facing or irreversible work should retain a human decision point.

concepts.title: Orchestration
concepts.evidence: Orchestration coordinates order, handoffs and shared state when more than one specialist or tool must contribute. It is unnecessary overhead for a task one agent can complete cleanly.

concepts.title: Multi-agent role separation
concepts.evidence: Assign different jobs—such as researcher, writer and reviewer—when independent contexts or perspectives improve the result. Define inputs, outputs and handoff contracts.

concepts.title: Observability
concepts.evidence: Require a visible record of steps, evidence and decisions so a human can understand what happened and diagnose a failure.

concepts.title: Stopping conditions
concepts.evidence: Every agent needs an explicit definition of done, failure, timeout or escalation; otherwise it may stop early or loop indefinitely.

concepts.title: Reusable skills
concepts.evidence: Turn a repeated, stable procedure into a reusable capability rather than rebuilding the instructions in every conversation. Creative or novel work may not benefit from rigid packaging.

images.meaning: Large concept cards/illustrations correspond to the 15 definitions; text must remain primary because some visuals repeat the prose.
images.review: Use only a representative diagram when it adds a mental model.

sources.title: 25 Claude Code Tips from 11 Months of Intense Use
sources.extractionQuality: medium; post body is readable, Reddit navigation interleaves text, comments are noisy

concepts.title: Customize the status line
concepts.evidence: Expose current model/session context and rate-limit information in the terminal so resource pressure is visible during work.

concepts.title: Learn essential slash commands
concepts.evidence: The post highlights built-in commands for context, usage and session control rather than treating the prompt box as the only interface.

concepts.title: Use voice for rich prompts
concepts.evidence: Dictation lowers the cost of providing goals, constraints and history. The author built separate live and prerecorded transcription workflows; commenters mention Windows Win+H and workplace restrictions on third-party voice tools.

concepts.title: Break large problems into smaller deliverables
concepts.evidence: Ask Claude to create or execute bounded pieces sequentially so each can be inspected and corrected before errors compound.

concepts.title: Use Git and GitHub CLI as the recovery/control layer
concepts.evidence: Let Claude inspect diffs, commits, issues and pull requests with git and gh. Commit coherent checkpoints so failed trajectories are recoverable and reviewable.

concepts.title: Keep context fresh and condensed
concepts.evidence: Context behaves like a perishable working set: stale history and raw output crowd out the current objective. Start fresh or compact around an explicit focus.

concepts.title: Capture terminal output
concepts.evidence: Pipe, redirect or capture command output so Claude can inspect it as evidence instead of relying on a human description.

concepts.title: Terminal aliases
concepts.evidence: Create short aliases for common Claude startup/resume combinations to reduce friction, while keeping flags understandable.

concepts.title: Compact proactively
concepts.evidence: Run compaction before context is nearly exhausted and tell the summarizer which goal, files, decisions and remaining work must survive.

concepts.title: Complete the write-test-observe cycle
concepts.evidence: For autonomous work, Claude must launch the program/test, send input, capture output and compare it with expectations. The tmux example creates a detached session, sends commands, captures the pane and terminates the session.
warnings: Prefer Playwright for browser-visible behavior instead of inferring UI success.

concepts.title: Efficiently edit long prompts
concepts.evidence: Use Cmd+A or Ctrl+A and terminal line-editing/navigation instead of laboriously deleting a bad prompt character by character.

concepts.title: Fallback retrieval for blocked sites
concepts.evidence: The post suggests a second CLI/model when a site blocks Claude's fetch path. Treat this as a retrieval fallback, validate provenance, and do not use it to evade access restrictions.
warnings: This is anecdotal tool advice, not an official Claude Code guarantee.

concepts.title: Invest in personal workflow tooling
concepts.evidence: Build or adapt the small tools that remove repeated friction—voice transcription, aliases, scripts and environment presets—rather than waiting for a universal workflow.

concepts.title: Search conversation history
concepts.evidence: Use saved local history or ask Claude to find prior discussion about a topic instead of re-explaining from memory.
concepts.prompt: What did we talk about regarding [topic] today?

concepts.title: Use terminal tabs for concurrent workstreams
concepts.evidence: Keep persistent utilities and independent tasks in separate named tabs so context and processes remain visible and do not interfere.

concepts.title: Slim the system prompt carefully
concepts.evidence: The author describes patching/removing generic system material to save context. This is an advanced, brittle optimization that can weaken safety or break after updates and should not be taught as a default practice.

concepts.title: Git worktrees for parallel branches
concepts.evidence: Create isolated working directories for concurrent Claude sessions so file edits do not collide while branches remain in one repository.

concepts.title: Manual exponential backoff
concepts.evidence: For long-running or rate-limited jobs, increase delays between retries and cap attempts rather than hammering the same operation.

concepts.title: Claude Code as a writing partner
concepts.evidence: Provide source material and an intended structure, draft in Markdown, review the diff and iterate. The filesystem makes versions and references inspectable.

concepts.title: Markdown as the interchange format
concepts.evidence: Use Markdown for portable structured notes, prompts, plans and drafts that are readable by humans, version control and Claude.

concepts.title: Preserve links when moving content
concepts.evidence: The author uses Notion as an intermediate destination because rich link context can be lost in some paste paths.

concepts.title: Isolate risky long-running automation
concepts.evidence: Run an inner Claude process in a container or dedicated machine, optionally controlled by an outer session through tmux. Isolation is the safety boundary when permissions are broad.
warnings: Never use broad permission bypass on the host or with valuable credentials/data.
Container isolation must include filesystem, secret and network boundaries.

concepts.title: Learn through sustained use
concepts.evidence: Workflow skill develops by noticing recurring friction, testing a change and retaining what works; reading tip lists is insufficient without deliberate practice.

concepts.title: Clone or half-clone conversations
concepts.evidence: Branch from a useful point to explore alternatives without contaminating the original trajectory; the post supplies a custom slash-command installation via symlink.

concepts.title: Use absolute paths
concepts.evidence: Resolve external file paths with realpath before referencing them so the agent and shell operate on the intended target.

concepts.title: Choose CLAUDE.md, skills, commands and plugins by lifecycle
concepts.evidence: CLAUDE.md carries project-wide persistent rules; a skill packages reusable domain knowledge/workflow; a slash command is an explicitly invoked prompt; a plugin distributes a bundle that may include skills, commands, hooks, agents or integrations.

discussionInsights.evidence: Readers ask how worktrees fit their IDE and how concurrent sessions should be coordinated; this signals a missing practical setup/cleanup lesson.
Commenters challenge whether users should manually trim context and note corporate restrictions on voice tools; present both convenience and governance constraints.
Discussion raises authorization boundaries, hooks/MCP messaging, background agents and deployment tasks; these comments are anecdotal and require safety labeling.
A long comment describes multi-model adversarial review, persistent context, lazy MCP routing and parallel specialist agents. It is a personal architecture, not validated product guidance.
A commenter adds a status-line topic hook to remind them of the session objective, a useful anti-drift pattern.

Terminal/code screenshots may support tmux automation, isolation and clone-command lessons; verify legibility before use.

sources.title: 27 Claude tips after 1,800 hours
sources.extractionQuality: medium; article readable but frequent separated characters and some paywall/video references

concepts.title: Do not overload Projects
concepts.evidence: Loading many files into a Project can make every answer a remix of broad context. Projects remain useful for stable, bounded corpora such as contracts or standard procedures; use targeted retrieval or a fresh context for other work.

concepts.title: Use stronger reasoning early, cheaper execution later
concepts.evidence: The author recommends a high-effort model for the initial direction, then switching to a less expensive capable model during execution. Model names are time-sensitive; retain the routing principle, not the exact product recommendation.
warnings: Specific model names/tiers may become obsolete.

concepts.title: Generate editable HTML infographics
concepts.evidence: Instead of asking for a raster image, provide a visual reference and ask Claude to code an HTML-like infographic. Benefits include editable layout and correctly rendered text.
concepts.prompt: Code an HTML-like infographic like the one I attached, but about [topic].

concepts.title: Edit the earlier prompt after a bad answer
concepts.evidence: Return to the prompt before the bad trajectory, improve it and regenerate, rather than adding repeated corrective messages to polluted context.

concepts.title: Dictate messy, comprehensive context
concepts.evidence: Speak the goal, constraints, attempts and desired result at length; end by telling Claude these are messy notes and to ask clarifying questions where needed.
concepts.prompt: These were messy voice notes. Ask me clarifying questions if you did not understand something.

concepts.title: Disable unused connectors
concepts.evidence: Keep only actively needed connectors enabled to reduce irrelevant tool choices and data exposure.

concepts.title: Start a fresh chat when performance degrades
concepts.evidence: Repeated correction and long histories can reduce quality. Preserve a concise handoff and restart instead of fighting accumulated mistakes.

concepts.title: Ask Claude to interview you
concepts.evidence: When requirements are unclear, ask Claude to pose targeted questions and offer selectable options before producing the artifact.

concepts.title: Prefer Code for artifact-building workflows
concepts.evidence: The author finds the Code surface more capable for building files/apps because it can work directly with a project. This is experiential, not a universal product comparison.

concepts.title: Use Cowork for broad parallel non-coding tasks
concepts.evidence: The article positions Cowork for large jobs where multiple Claude workers can prepare deliverables in parallel; small tasks may not justify it.
warnings: Product surface and behavior are time-sensitive.

concepts.title: Configure Cowork with a setup skill
concepts.evidence: A setup-cowork skill interviews the user about preferences, styles and working methods to create reusable configuration.

concepts.title: Send screenshots instead of vague visual descriptions
concepts.evidence: A screenshot communicates layout, spacing and visual hierarchy more directly than prose; pair it with explicit comparison and verification instructions.

concepts.title: Build personalized mini-apps
concepts.evidence: Turn recurring personal data or decisions into small interactive artifacts rather than repeatedly asking for static prose.

concepts.title: Embed Claude in a mini-app
concepts.evidence: The article demonstrates an artifact that includes Claude-backed interaction and can be shared by link. Treat external sharing and data access as security design concerns.

concepts.title: Team seat-count advice
concepts.evidence: The author recommends staying under a particular seat threshold; this is commercial/time-sensitive and lacks enough durable technical rationale for a mastery lesson.

concepts.title: Combine connectors for cross-system synthesis
concepts.evidence: For a substantial email, combine Slack context, Drive documents and other authorized sources so the output reflects multiple systems. Minimize connector scope and verify citations.

concepts.title: Provide negative preference feedback
concepts.evidence: Tell Claude specifically what style or behavior you dislike so it can revise and, where appropriate, encode a durable preference.

concepts.title: Open and work from Drive files
concepts.evidence: Use an authorized Drive connector to ground work in existing files rather than copying fragments manually.

concepts.title: Vibecoding is not a business model
concepts.evidence: Fast app generation does not replace product discovery, distribution, reliability, security or willingness-to-pay. Teach outcome validation alongside code generation.

concepts.title: Skills are for repeated tasks
concepts.evidence: Package repeatable, stable procedures as skills; do not constrain genuinely creative or one-off work with an over-specific template.

concepts.title: Research-mode skepticism
concepts.evidence: The author reports low usage of a named Research mode. This is opinion and product telemetry is not supplied; do not present it as fact.

concepts.title: Make data interactive
concepts.evidence: Convert analysis into a small interface where the user can filter, compare or test scenarios rather than delivering a static report only.

concepts.title: Remove generic AI writing signals
concepts.evidence: Use concrete voice, source-specific details and editorial revision rather than accepting generic polished prose.

concepts.title: Avoid technique-chasing
concepts.evidence: The author dismisses trend-driven jargon such as loop engineering. Reconcile this with the engineering source: ignore jargon for simple personal work, but bounded loops and observability matter for unattended production systems.

concepts.title: Do not constantly switch tools
concepts.evidence: Depth with one primary tool can beat repeated migration driven by hype; use another tool when a concrete requirement justifies it.

concepts.title: Enterprise safety comparison claim
concepts.evidence: The author makes a broad safety comparison tied to Google usage. The PDF does not provide a formal security analysis; exclude the claim or label it opinion.

concepts.title: AI-assisted mathematical discovery anecdote
concepts.evidence: A closing anecdote illustrates rapidly expanding capability but does not translate into a Claude Code operating practice without external verification.

images.meaning: Product UI and worked artifact screenshots can support Projects, model routing, screenshot prompting, connectors and mini-app lessons.

uncertainties: Some referenced videos are unavailable in the PDF body.

concepts.title: Claude Code as a research tool

concepts.title: Use multiple verification modes

concepts.title: Choose the right abstraction level

sources.title: Best practices for Claude Code
sources.extractionQuality: high content coverage with mojibake ligatures

concepts.title: Context is the fundamental constraint
concepts.evidence: Conversation messages, files and command output all consume context; quality can degrade as it fills. Track usage and treat every read/output as spending a finite reasoning resource.

concepts.title: Give Claude an executable verification target
concepts.evidence: Provide tests, build/lint exit codes, fixture diffs or screenshot comparisons. Ask for evidence—the command and output—not a success assertion. Escalation options are prompt-level iteration, /goal, deterministic Stop hooks, and fresh-context verification subagents.
prompts: Write a validateEmail function. Example cases: user@example.com is true, invalid is false, user@.com is false. Run tests after implementing.
[Paste screenshot] Implement this design, take a screenshot, compare it to the original, list differences and fix them.
Fix the supplied build error, verify the build succeeds, and address the root cause rather than suppressing it.

concepts.title: Explore, plan, implement, commit
concepts.evidence: Use plan mode to read relevant code and constraints without changes, create/edit a plan, implement with tests, then commit/open a PR. Skip planning overhead when the entire diff is obvious and small.

concepts.title: Provide specific context
concepts.evidence: Name the file, scenario, constraints, existing pattern and desired verification. Reference files with @, paste images, provide URLs, pipe data or instruct Claude to retrieve needed context with Bash/MCP.

concepts.title: Write an effective CLAUDE.md
concepts.evidence: Run /init for a baseline, then retain commands, style and workflow rules Claude cannot infer. Keep it short and human-readable; test with /context, prune low-value lines, use emphasis sparingly and import supporting files with @path.

concepts.title: Configure permissions by risk
concepts.evidence: Use auto mode for classification, /permissions for known commands and domains, and /sandbox for OS isolation. Default prompts guard file writes, Bash and MCP actions; allowlist repeated safe operations rather than bypassing all checks.

concepts.title: Prefer CLI, connect MCP where it adds capability
concepts.evidence: CLIs are context-efficient for external services; install gh for GitHub. Add MCP servers for systems such as Notion, Figma or databases when structured integration is needed.

concepts.title: Use hooks for invariants and skills for reusable expertise
concepts.evidence: Hooks deterministically run scripts at lifecycle events and are appropriate for zero-exception checks or blocks. Skills under .claude/skills package domain knowledge and workflows.
prompts: Write a hook that runs eslint after every file edit.
Write a hook that blocks writes to the migrations folder.

concepts.title: End-to-end GitHub issue workflow
concepts.evidence: Fetch the issue, understand it, search relevant code, implement, test, lint/type-check, write a descriptive commit, push and open a PR.

concepts.title: Custom subagents and plugins
concepts.evidence: Subagents have isolated context and tool permissions; delegate file-heavy investigation or specialist review and request line-specific fixes. Plugins bundle skills, hooks, subagents and MCP; typed-language code-intelligence plugins improve symbol navigation.

concepts.title: Interview and specification workflow
concepts.evidence: For ambiguous substantial work, ask Claude to interview the user, write a specification/plan to a file, review it, then execute in a fresh session with clean context.

concepts.title: Stop, rewind and clear
concepts.evidence: Esc stops mid-action while preserving context. Esc twice or /rewind restores conversation, code, both, or summarizes from a checkpoint. /clear resets unrelated or correction-polluted work; after more than two failed corrections, restart with a better prompt.

concepts.title: Aggressive but deliberate context management
concepts.evidence: Use /clear between tasks, /compact with preservation instructions, partial rewind/summarize for selected history, CLAUDE.md compaction rules for critical file/test state, and /btw for disposable questions that should not enter history.

concepts.title: Keep investigation out of the main context
concepts.evidence: Delegate broad codebase exploration to subagents; they return a compact finding set. Also use a fresh subagent to check edge cases after implementation.
prompts: Use subagents to investigate how authentication handles token refresh.
Use a subagent to review this code for edge cases.

concepts.title: Name and resume sessions
concepts.evidence: Treat named sessions like workstream branches. Continue the latest with claude --continue or choose one with claude --resume; checkpoints survive closing and resuming.

concepts.title: Non-interactive automation
concepts.evidence: Use claude -p in scripts, CI or hooks; choose machine-readable output and scope tools. Session persistence is default unless disabled.

concepts.title: Parallel sessions by coordination need
concepts.evidence: Options range from manual worktrees and desktop-managed sessions to cloud sessions and coordinated agent teams. Isolate edits, assign non-overlapping ownership and use writer/reviewer separation for quality.

concepts.title: Fan-out batch work
concepts.evidence: Call claude -p for independent items, constrain allowed tools, collect structured outputs and synthesize only after all workers finish. Suitable for large migrations or analyses with separable units.

concepts.title: Fresh-context diff review
concepts.evidence: Have a subagent review the diff against explicit criteria or PLAN.md, or run the bundled code-review skill. A reviewer without the implementing rationale is more likely to notice unjustified assumptions.
prompts: Use a subagent to review the rate limiter diff against PLAN.md and report gaps.

concepts.title: Common failure patterns
concepts.evidence: Avoid kitchen-sink sessions, repeated corrections, overlong CLAUDE.md, trust without verification, and unbounded investigation. Fix with clear task boundaries, fresh context, pruning, executable checks and subagents.

concepts.title: Develop judgment from observed outcomes
concepts.evidence: Notice which prompt structure, context and mode produced good work; diagnose failures; learn when accumulated history is valuable versus when it is noise.

images.meaning: Tables and workflow diagrams are meaningful; prioritize the verification table, explore-plan-code sequence, memory hierarchy, session controls and parallel-session comparison.

uncertainties: The saved official document reflects 2026 features such as /goal, auto mode and /btw; product availability must be labeled by document date.
Mojibake affects ligatures but not overall meaning.

sources.title: Claude Code Ralph Loop: From Basic Prompts to Autonomous Overnight Builds
sources.extractionQuality: high narrative coverage; code line wrapping and screenshot text require PDF consultation

concepts.title: Ralph core loop
concepts.evidence: Ralph repeatedly sends a prompt to Claude rather than accepting the first perceived completion. Failure is expected; artifacts left in files become evidence for the next iteration. The basic historical form is a Bash while loop; the Anthropic plugin form uses a Stop hook.

concepts.title: Verification and fresh-context rationale
concepts.evidence: Claude can stop when code looks complete and degrade as a long context fills. Ralph forces a completion signal tied to checks and lets each iteration inspect durable files from a cleaner context.

concepts.title: Stop-hook flow
concepts.evidence: Prompt plus completion promise enters the loop; Claude works and attempts to exit; the hook scans output; absent promise causes the prompt to be fed back; present promise ends the run.

concepts.title: Three-part state architecture
concepts.evidence: prd.json stores atomic tasks and passes flags; progress.txt is short-term iteration memory; agents.md stores longer-lived project patterns. This separates task truth, run notes and durable knowledge.

concepts.title: Completion promise must encode real done
concepts.evidence: The promise is only safe when the prompt defines binary, independently verifiable criteria. A vague promise creates an expensive loop or premature success; require tests and task flags before emitting it.

concepts.title: What Ralph is not
concepts.evidence: It is not magic, not a substitute for task design, not identical to every loop implementation and not appropriate for every task. Use it for complex multi-step work with verifiable completion.

concepts.title: Generate and review a PRD
concepts.evidence: Describe product goal, users, scope, constraints, acceptance criteria and non-goals; have Claude structure the PRD, then review it before task generation.

concepts.title: Atomic task list in prd.json
concepts.evidence: Break the PRD into small priority-ordered tasks with stable IDs, descriptions, acceptance criteria and passes:false. Each iteration selects one incomplete item and changes the flag only after checks pass.

concepts.title: Progress log
concepts.evidence: Append concise work completed, tests, failures, blockers and next-step learning after each iteration. Do not turn the file into a full transcript.

concepts.title: Durable agents.md knowledge
concepts.evidence: Promote stable codebase patterns or constraints from run notes into durable agent guidance; avoid storing temporary sprint state there.

concepts.title: Feedback loops inside the prompt
concepts.evidence: Require tests, type checks and lint after each bounded change. The agent must read failures and correct them before marking a task passed.

concepts.title: Iteration and cost controls
concepts.evidence: Set max iterations, begin with a small attended run, monitor token cost and stop on repeated non-progress. Autonomous execution needs safe permissions and rollbackable commits.

concepts.title: Level 1: single supervised iteration
concepts.evidence: Watch one iteration end-to-end to learn artifact changes, test behavior, failure shape and token cost before automating repetition.

concepts.title: Level 2: attended loop
concepts.evidence: Run a bounded multi-iteration loop while checking task flags, progress updates and emerging patterns. Pause and repair the prompt/PRD when drift appears. Advance only after several observed loops and many iterations.

concepts.title: Level 3: unattended overnight
concepts.evidence: Prerequisites include a proven attended history, atomic PRD, built-in tests/types/lint, restricted environment, rollback points, max iterations (article suggests 30-50), and notification. Morning review checks prd.json, progress.txt, git history, tests and the feature; 100% completion is not assumed.

concepts.title: Pattern 1: feature builder
concepts.evidence: Select highest-priority passes:false task, implement only it, run checks, set passes:true only on success, append progress and emit COMPLETE only when all tasks pass.

concepts.title: Pattern 2: test-until-green
concepts.evidence: Add or repair tests in tiny units, run coverage/test feedback and improve one function per iteration so failures stay attributable.

concepts.title: Pattern 3: multi-persona review
concepts.evidence: Review the same artifact through roles such as security engineer, solution architect and QA; record findings and corrections. Personas are perspectives inside a controlled loop, not proof of correctness.

concepts.title: Pattern 4: proof-of-concept validator
concepts.evidence: Prioritize whether the risky architectural idea works; explicitly defer comprehensive tests and edge handling until viability is established. Use for architecture validation, not production readiness.

concepts.title: Choose and combine patterns
concepts.evidence: Match the loop to the outcome: feature builder for scoped delivery, test-until-green for coverage, multi-persona for review breadth, POC for uncertainty reduction. Patterns can be sequenced, such as build then review.

sources.extractionQuality: high with ligature mojibake and page-layout line mixing

concepts.title: CLAUDE.md as project-level system context
concepts.evidence: CLAUDE.md tells Claude what code alone cannot: stack, structure, commands, conventions and boundaries. Instructions have persistent high priority, so every line consumes attention and 'less is more.'

concepts.title: Three-part mental model
concepts.evidence: Project memory preserves setup across sessions; operational boundaries state rules not to break; context primer prevents a blank start.

concepts.title: Hierarchical loading
concepts.evidence: Global, project-root and nested directory CLAUDE.md files layer instructions. A monorepo can keep shared rules at root and backend/frontend-specific rules near their code.

concepts.title: Organize content as WHY, HOW and WHAT
concepts.evidence: WHY explains purpose/architecture, HOW supplies commands and workflows, WHAT lists critical conventions and boundaries. Example material includes API prefixes, formatting, tests and schema conventions.

concepts.title: Less is more
concepts.evidence: Overlong instructions compete and become stale. Keep key folders, commands and bug-causing conventions; remove onboarding prose and information discoverable from the repository.

concepts.title: Progressive disclosure with agent_docs
concepts.evidence: Keep a concise index in CLAUDE.md that points to focused documents for testing, database work or deployment; load detail only when the task needs it.

concepts.title: Three creation methods
concepts.evidence: Generate a baseline with /init, create manually for precise control, and use # during work to capture newly discovered rules. Recommended sequence: /init, manual refinement, continuous additions with later pruning.

concepts.title: Clear Markdown sections
concepts.evidence: Use headers for project map, commands, conventions, testing and constraints so unrelated instructions do not bleed together.

concepts.title: Encode repeatable workflows
concepts.evidence: For endpoint creation and database migrations, specify ordered steps including analogous-code search, schema/model changes, implementation, tests, documentation, upgrade and rollback checks.

concepts.title: Context-specific instruction files
concepts.evidence: Distinct phases or areas can have scoped rules—development/deployment, frontend/backend—and MCP guidance can state read-only production access and prohibit writes.

concepts.title: Hooks enforce deterministic rules
concepts.evidence: Use hooks for formatting, validation or prohibitions that must run every time; do not spend model reasoning on deterministic operations.

concepts.title: CLAUDE.md primes subagents
concepts.evidence: Specialist subagents run in isolated contexts; concise project instructions let them understand conventions without inheriting the full main conversation.

concepts.title: Maintain CLAUDE.md as code
concepts.evidence: Update with PRs, capture discoveries using #, review quarterly, remove stale material, commit to version control and include instruction review in the PR checklist.

concepts.title: CLAUDE.md, hooks, subagents and MCP are complementary
concepts.evidence: CLAUDE.md establishes rules/context; hooks execute invariants; subagents isolate specialist work; MCP extends access. Do not collapse all four into one mechanism.

images.meaning: Hierarchy diagrams, templates, example files, /init/# UI, workflow snippets and hooks/subagent diagrams are highly relevant. Use readable crops with page attribution.

uncertainties: The title promises hooks/subagents/pro automation, but most depth is CLAUDE.md; hooks and subagents receive introductory rather than exhaustive treatment.
Some code blocks lose indentation in text extraction.

sources.title: Graphify + Obsidian + Claude Code = CHEAT CODE
sources.extractionQuality: low-to-medium text density; workflow is primarily visual

concepts.title: File-by-file search misses relationships
concepts.evidence: A directory of many disconnected documents forces repeated search and obscures links among ideas. A graph layer makes connections and central concepts visible.

concepts.title: Acquire an authoritative corpus
concepts.evidence: The example asks Claude Code to download official Claude Code documentation before graphing it. The run reportedly retrieves 171 pages and self-corrects a coding error; source quality matters more than graph appearance.
concepts.prompt: Download the official Claude Code docs, map them with Graphify, then turn that into an Obsidian knowledge base.

concepts.title: Graphify documents into connected concepts
concepts.evidence: Graphify represents ideas as nodes and relationships as links; larger connected nodes can indicate centrality. A graph is a navigation aid, not proof that a concept is important or correct.

concepts.title: Generate an Obsidian vault
concepts.evidence: Convert each idea into an individual linked note. Begin in a separate disposable vault so generated structure can be inspected or removed safely before merging into personal notes.

concepts.title: Repair bare or weakly connected notes
concepts.evidence: Inspect the graph for unhelpful nodes or missing relationships and give a focused correction prompt rather than accepting the first generated network.

concepts.title: Link every note to source documents
concepts.evidence: Copy/source the underlying documents and add backlinks so each synthesized note can be traced to evidence. Without provenance, a polished graph becomes an unverifiable derivative.
concepts.prompt: Pull the source docs in and link every note back to where it came from.

concepts.title: Merge as an isolated folder
concepts.evidence: After review, place the generated vault inside the main vault in its own folder, preserving a simple rollback/delete boundary.
concepts.prompt: Put this vault inside my main vault, in its own folder.

concepts.title: Knowledge graphs need a revisit policy
concepts.evidence: The closing discussion asks how users decide what to revisit daily or weekly. The source does not answer; the curriculum should add review queues, freshness and orphan-note checks as instructor synthesis.

images.meaning: The source is visual: tool pages, generated graph, command result, isolated vault and provenance links. Screenshots are necessary to teach this workflow, but text must describe every action.

uncertainties: Very low body word count because screenshots carry much of the evidence.
Exact Graphify installation and plugin provenance are not fully captured in readable text.
Claims about retrieved page counts and self-correction are author-reported.

concepts.title: Tips 0-31: expanded canonical YK set

concepts.title: Use auto mode
concepts.evidence: Let the permission classifier approve low-risk actions while preserving review for risky operations; this reduces approval fatigue without a blanket bypass.

concepts.title: Control Claude Code from a phone
concepts.evidence: Remote control can keep long-running work accessible away from the desktop, but requires authenticated transport, session isolation and protection against exposed terminals.

concepts.title: Use artifacts
concepts.evidence: Build inspectable interactive outputs instead of prose when the task benefits from exploration, sharing or visualization.

concepts.title: Write many tests and use TDD
concepts.evidence: Write tests first, confirm they fail, commit them, then implement until they pass. Tests give the agent a durable objective signal and make autonomous iteration safer.

concepts.title: Be braver in unknown code through iteration
concepts.evidence: Use checkpoints and verification to attempt unfamiliar work, inspect failure and iterate; do not confuse courage with unbounded production risk.

concepts.title: Run Bash commands and subagents in background
concepts.evidence: Parallelize independent investigations or long commands while the main session continues. Track ownership and collect results before integration.

concepts.title: Personalized software
concepts.evidence: Low-cost generation makes narrow tools for an individual workflow practical; retain maintainability and data-safety expectations.

concepts.title: Navigate and edit the input box
concepts.evidence: Learn multiline input, cursor movement, selection and history so detailed prompts can be edited before submission rather than corrected afterward.

concepts.title: Plan, but prototype quickly
concepts.evidence: Use planning where dependencies/risk justify it, and a small reversible prototype where uncertainty is best resolved by evidence. Planning and prototyping are complementary.

concepts.title: Simplify overcomplicated code
concepts.evidence: After achieving correctness, ask Claude to identify unnecessary abstraction and reduce complexity while preserving behavior through tests.

concepts.title: Automation of automation
concepts.evidence: When a repeated manual process is stable, ask Claude to create the script, hook or skill that automates future instances; validate the automation on a bounded case.

concepts.title: Share knowledge
concepts.evidence: Document useful workflows and contribute improvements so team practice compounds rather than remaining private prompt lore.

concepts.title: Keep learning
concepts.evidence: Treat techniques as hypotheses and update the operating manual as product capabilities and observed results change.
